input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Computed parameters (the document spells these in words, which is why a digit-based scan returns "number not found"; there is no numeric gap): (1) non-renewal notice window = "thirty days" = 30 days, which is <= the preferred 30 days and well inside the 60-day fallback and the 90-day walk-away; (2) renewal term = "successive twelve-month periods" = 12 months, so no automatic multi-year renewal; (3) Vendor renewal reminder = "at least sixty days" = 60 days before renewal, and if the reminder is missed Customer's opt-out deadline is tolled to 30 days after receipt; (4) renewal uplift = lesser of trailing 12-month CPI-U and "three percent" = 3%, with 90 days' notice of any increase and no increase on prepaid periods. All four parameters meet the preferred position, so no redline is proposed and the paragraphs are returned unchanged. Non-renewal is Customer's right alone, an asymmetry in our favour that we do not flag. Section 2.1's 3-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" may blunt the practical value of the opt-out, but that is a minimum-commitment/termination-rights issue for the relevant commitment rule, not a defect in the renewal mechanics.
